 Order

Present miscellaneous appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicle Act is filed against the award dated 24.01.2023 passed by Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior in Claim Case No.811/2022.

The facts in brief to decide this appeal in brief are that the appellants - claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 r/w Sec. 140 of Motor Vehicles Act before the learned Claims Tribunal for claiming the compensation on account of death of their son-Purusottam Dhakad in a road traffic accident occurred on 04.04.2022 involving motorcycle bearing registration No. MP 33 MS 6831.
Respondents No. 1 and 2 - owner and driver of the offending vehicle filed written statements and denied the allegations made in the claim petition.

Respondent No. 3 - Insurance Company of the offending vehicle also filed its written statement and denied the allegations made in the claim petition stating therein that the offending vehicle was being plied in violation of the policy terms and conditions, therefore, insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

Learned claims tribunal framed issues and after recording the evidence of both the parties awarded compensation to the appellants / claimants to the tune of Rs.12,65,810/- with interest @ 6% P.A.
from the date of filing of the claim petition.
The appellants/claimants has taken the grounds for appeal that learned Claims Tribunal has wrongly assessed the monthly income as Rs.8325/- ignoring the fact that he was the driver of heavy vehicle.

The learned claims tribunal should have assessed the amount of Rs.11360/- as per M.P.
State Legal Services Authority guidelines.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent No.3- Insurance Company argued that on the basis of the fact and circumstances as well as evidence adduced on record, learned Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the deceased.

He further argued that guidelines issued by M.P.
State Legal Services Authority are not binding on the Courts and the income should be assessed on the basis of the evidence adduced on record.
Any guidelines issued for Lok Adalats do not have the binding effects.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the available record.

The claimant-Suresh (AW/1), who is father of the deceased stated that his son (deceased-Purusottam) was a driver at the time of accident and was earning of Rs.15,000/- pm.
However, the claimant has failed to file any documents to prove that his son was working as a driver.
He has also failed to give the details of employer under whom the deceased was working as a driver.

In these circumstances when there is no corroborative evidence, merely on the basis of the driving license of heavy motor vehicle, it cannot be said that the deceased was working as a driver and was getting Rs.15,000/- per month as salary.
On the basis of evidence adduced by the claimants, learned Claims Tribunal has rightly calculated the income of the deceased as Rs.8,325/- pm.

Under these circumstances, in light of the evidence adduced and settled principle of law, the compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is found to be just and proper and therefore, no interference is warranted in the impugned award.
Consequently, the appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE (LJ*)
